text:
sarah: Hey team, escalating a customer issue hitting embeddings endpoint. They upgraded our TS SDK and now see sporadic dimension mismatches under load. example: expected 768 but response vectors are length 1536 intermittently.
dev-support-bot: Ticket created: INC-7782. Assigned to support oncall.
jordan: Which SDK versions and model? Any reproducible request payload?

sarah: Customer stack: python-sdk v1.3.0 for ingestion, ts-sdk v0.11.2 for inference, model pinned to redwood/emb-small-768. Happens during high-throughput batch runs (~120-250 rps). I pasted a minimal repro (TS) below.

sarah: ```ts
import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
const texts = new Array(16).fill('search query')
const res = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood/emb-small-768', input: texts })
console.log(res.data[0].embedding.length)
```

mike: Any error codes in responses? 400/500? Or is the API returning valid 200 but wrong vector length?

sarah: Always 200. No error field. Just the vector length toggles between 768 and 1536. Happens more when concurrency > 40. Attached short server logs from customer showing warnings.

sarah: ```
2026-03-09T14:12:51Z WARN batcher: merged requests 8->1, expected_dim=768, out_dim=1536, model_variant=quant-2x
2026-03-09T14:12:51Z INFO runtime: serving shard gpu-3
2026-03-09T14:12:52Z INFO kvcache: served prefix hit rate 0.12
```

anna: That log line looks like a batch-merge double-pack issue. Could be when two model variants (fp16 + q4_0) are pooled by the batcher and post-process concatenates embeddings accidentally.

jordan: Can you confirm if the customer is using a mixed-model routing policy or model alias that can route to a 1536-dim model? If routing maps redwood/emb-small-768 -> fallback emb-medium-1536 under load, that could explain it.

sarah: They said model is pinned. Console shows pinned: redwood/emb-small-768. No fallbacks configured. Also saw this on Dedicated environment where fallback routing shouldn't occur.

mike: Two hypotheses: (1) batcher buffer reuse causing output buffer from previous larger-dim response to be reused for smaller model, (2) SDK client-side concatenation when it receives multiple partial shards and merges wrongly under streaming.

anna: Is the issue present across languages? They reported from TS inference, python ingestion. Could be server-side but we should test both client SDKs.

jordan: Quick local repro steps for eng to try:
- start staging runtime with --batch-size 16 --enable-shard-reuse-checks
- run a mixed concurrent load: 60 concurrent clients sending 4 requests each
- run both TS and Python SDK calls in parallel
- monitor logs for "expected_dim" warnings

mike: I'll spin up a repro in staging now. If it's buffer reuse, adding a defensive zeroing of the out buffer or assert on dims should surface it.

sarah: Customer requests a mitigation: they can temporarily set max_concurrency to 30 on their client. Also asked about SDK pin recommendations.

jordan: If it's server side, pinning won't help. But we can recommend downgrading TS SDK to 0.10.x if you suspect a client merge bug. Need to verify.

mike: Repro started. Initial run: sending 1000 embed requests over 2 mins. Seeing a few recreates: "WARN batcher: output_dim_mismatch expected=768 got=1536". Reproduced.

mike: Stacktrace from staging runtime:
```
runtime/serve/batcher.go:412: func mergeBatches -> panic? not panic but log
runtime/transform/postprocess.go:78: func pack_embeddings -> len(dst)=1536, len(src)=768
```

anna: That's server-side. Assigning to eng-runtime. @jordan can you triage kernel/packing code? Looks like postprocess packer uses batch_size*max_dim as target but doesn't check model-specific dim.

jordan: Aha. I recall a change to reuse output arrays for speed — likely forgot to assert per-request num_dimensions. I'll add a guard and a metric for dim_mismatch_count. Also adding a config flag to disable reuse: runtime.disable_output_reuse=false by default, will set to true in a hotfix for affected clusters.

sarah: Customer asked about timeline. They need a mitigation ASAP — will apply client-side throttle for now but want a server fix.

mike: Hotfix plan: patch postprocess to validate dims and refuse to merge requests across different model_dim. Canary deploy to staging then to affected Dedicated pool. ETA 3-6 hours for patch + canary.

dev-support-bot: Incident note appended to INC-7782: hotfix planned, eng-runtime owner @jordan.

anna: Also adding an observability alert rule: if embedding_dim_mismatch_rate > 0.1% over 5m then page oncall.

sarah: Perfect. I'll relay workaround to customer: set client max_concurrency 25 and pin SDK to ts-sdk@0.10.9 while we hotfix. Also please provide a short postmortem once done.

jordan: Will post PR link and small changelog when ready. PR will include unit tests reproducing dim mismatch.

mike: After patch, re-run the staging workload. Verified no dim mismatch over 30k requests.

sarah: Customer confirmed reduced errors after throttle. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

anna: Leaving this thread open until patch rolled to prod. Adding follow-ups for telemetry and SDK release notes.
